qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Automotive and industrial qualification cycles (AEC-Q100, functional safety) create meaningful design-in switching costs across multi-year vehicle platforms. However, power semiconductors lack pricing power >= inflation, facing mandatory annual OEM price-downs and aggressive price deflation in Silicon Carbide (SiC) from surging Chinese capacity. Primary erosion threats: state-subsidized Chinese SiC wafer/module competition, cyclical auto/industrial demand swings, and commoditization of power discretes.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Pricing Power & Proof of Moat, REJECT). While onsemi benefits from sticky automotive design-in qualification cycles, it lacks pricing power >= inflation across the cycle. Auto and industrial OEMs continuously extract annual price-downs, and aggressive capacity expansion by Chinese SiC competitors has led to sharp wafer/device price deflation, forcing onsemi to curtail capex and fab expansions. Multi-cycle returns on capital remain volatile with GAAP operating margins plunging to ~1.4% in the 2025 cyclical trough.
qualitative.evidence: Fiscal 2025 revenue fell 15.3% YoY to $6.0B (from $7.08B in 2024 and $8.25B in 2023 peak) due to broad automotive and industrial inventory destocking. GAAP operating margin compressed from ~25% in 2024 to 1.4% in 2025 ($84M operating income) under fab underutilization and manufacturing realignment charges. Trailing ROIC dropped to single digits (~8.9%). Despite solid FCF ($1.4B in 2025 via capex pacing and working capital release) and conservative balance sheet management, power discretes and SiC suffer structural price deflation and commoditization risks from low-cost Chinese competitors, failing the Munger standard for pricing power.
